tldr: DeepSeek shipped V4.1-Flash on Sep 10, claiming it beats flagship V4-Pro while cutting the memory agents need to run it. The efficiency claim rattled Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron shares within a day, and DeepSeek quantified it Sep 13 as a 75% HBM and 87.5% SSD cut.
whats_new: A Sep 27 shattered.io write-up claims V4.1-Flash beats Anthropic's Opus 5 at 70% lower cost -- the fifth benchmark comparison in this series since launch, now aimed at a Western flagship instead of DeepSeek's own prior models, still with no independent verification.
why_it_matters: Anyone calling the V4-Pro endpoint is now served different weights than they pinned, at a price that keeps falling, without a version bump to signal either change -- and now a third-party host serves the same model, so routing choices need re-checking too.

status.state: Shipped · V4-Pro traffic silently rerouted, now on third-party hosts too
status.detail: V4.1-Flash launched Sep 10 beating V4-Pro on quality while cutting agent memory needs; the efficiency claim rattled memory-chip stocks by Sep 11, and by Sep 14 DeepSeek was routing all V4-Pro traffic to V4.1-Flash at a falling price. Sep 20-27 added architecture specifics, third-party hosting, and a run of benchmark claims culminating in a Sep 27 claim of beating Opus 5 at 70% lower cost.

beats.headline: DeepSeek unveils V4.1-Flash, claims it beats flagship V4-Pro
beats.summary: The new model launches as an upgrade over DeepSeek's own current flagship.

beats.headline: Cuts agent memory needs and slashes agentic costs by 80%
Efficiency claim rattles Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron shares
beats.summary: Multiple outlets tie the memory-savings claim to a same-day dip in memory-chip stocks.

beats.headline: Benchmark series widens from Chinese rivals to a Western flagship
beats.summary: A Sep 17 benchmark puts the coding gap at 11 points over Qwen3-Coder and Devstral, a Sep 20 follow-up adds architecture specifics (a 1M-token context window via extreme KV-cache compression), a Sep 25 write-up claims a 4.4x gap over V4-Pro and V4-Flash, and a Sep 27 piece from the same benchmark series claims V4.1-Flash beats Anthropic's Opus 5 at 70% lower cost.

beats.headline: DeepSeek puts numbers on the memory cut: 75% less HBM, 87.5% less SSD
DeepSeek quietly swaps V4-Pro traffic for V4.1-Flash at Flash pricing
beats.summary: Four days after launch, calls to the V4-Pro endpoint are served by V4.1-Flash instead, billed at the cheaper Flash rate.

beats.headline: 552B-parameter spec surfaces as a community uncensored fine-tune racks up downloads
Cached-input pricing drops again to $0.003 per million tokens
ZenMux adds V4.1-Flash for high-throughput reasoning
beats.summary: First sign the model is spreading to inference platforms beyond DeepSeek's own API.

open_questions: Does the claimed memory-footprint cut hold up in independent agent-workload benchmarks, not just DeepSeek's own numbers?
Will DeepSeek formally deprecate the V4-Pro endpoint, or keep serving V4.1-Flash under the old name indefinitely?
Do outputs from the V4-Pro endpoint show measurable quality or behavior differences now that V4.1-Flash serves them?
Has the 1M-token context and KV-cache compression figure been independently benchmarked, or does it restate DeepSeek's own claims?
Does ZenMux serve the identical weights and config as DeepSeek's own endpoint, or a re-quantized variant with different behavior?
Does the claimed edge over Opus 5 hold up under independent benchmarking, given the same content series already ran four unverified DeepSeek-internal comparisons?
take_for_builders: Re-run your eval suite against the V4-Pro endpoint: you're getting V4.1-Flash's outputs at a still-falling price, and any prompt or behavior tuned to V4-Pro specifically may have silently drifted. If you route through ZenMux or another third-party host, verify it serves the same weights before trusting cross-provider evals.
